Summer22.title: Muons and electrons both 3–5% low, same as last time
Summer22.body: With 0.39 fb⁻¹ in Z→ee and 0.74 fb⁻¹ in Z→μμ, data/MC after the full selection is 0.95 ± 0.01 (Z→ee) and 0.97 ± 0.01 (Z→μμ). Both channels are low by a similar amount, so this looks like normalization (DY cross section, luminosity), not leptons. WW is now included. The Z→ee peak now has the same width in data and MC. DY + b is about 4% and DY + c about 8% of the DY events.
next: Muon trigger SF from both muons, like the electrons now. Needs MC trigger efficiencies, which MUO does not provide.
Full run on condor to get the pileup and jet-multiplicity shapes right (20 data files is too few).
b/c-tag SFs once we cut on the tagger; decide what to do without c-tag shape SFs.

Summer22EE.title: Data and MC agree within 3% in both channels
Summer22EE.body: With 0.63 fb⁻¹ in Z→ee and 0.84 fb⁻¹ in Z→μμ, data/MC after the full selection is 0.97 ± 0.01 (Z→ee) and 0.99 ± 0.01 (Z→μμ). Z→ee moved down by 1.5% because the trigger SF now uses both electrons. Electrons are low in both endcaps (about 0.95), as expected after the 2022 ECAL endcap issue. The Z→ee peak now has the same width in data and MC. This campaign is in good shape.

Summer23.body: With 0.60 fb⁻¹ in each channel (Muon0 and EGamma0, half of their luminosity), data/MC after the full selection is 0.97 ± 0.01 (Z→ee) and 0.99 ± 0.01 (Z→μμ). All 20 EGamma files were read this time. The Z→ee peak now has the same width in data and MC. This campaign is in good shape.

Summer23BPix.title: Muons agree within 1%, electrons are 6% low, mostly at negative η
Summer23BPix.body: With 0.62 fb⁻¹ in each channel, data/MC is 0.99 ± 0.01 in Z→μμ but 0.94 ± 0.01 in Z→ee. The electron deficit grows towards negative η: 0.98 in the positive endcap, 0.90 in the negative endcap. Muons show nothing like it. Before SFs, Z→ee data/MC is 0.97. The 2023D electron ID SFs are above 1 and push the MC up, while in 2022 they push it down. So the electron SFs for 2023D are the place to look. The Z→ee peak width is now within 3% of data.
